states.active: The current task. Only one feature may be active at a time.
states.blocked: Cannot continue until a documented blocker is resolved.

features.behavior: Running bin/harness-audit.sh against any repo prints a score out of a stable denominator, lists every failing check with an actionable fix, and exits 1 when a critical check fails.
verification: Run bin/harness-audit.sh on a bare repo — expect critical failures and exit 1.
Run it on a fully scaffolded repo — expect 7/7 critical and exit 0.
Confirm the total is identical for both (comparable scores).

layers.label: static
layers.repair: Fix the reported syntax error. The script must stay bash 3.2 compatible: no associative arrays, no ${var,,}.

layers.label: runtime
layers.repair: JSON output is malformed. Check json_escape handles quotes and backslashes in every check description and fix string.

evidence: tests/run-tests.sh sections 2-3 and 12 pass — stable denominator and parseable JSON confirmed 2026-08-05
features.notes: 74 checks across the five subsystems plus L03-L12.

features.behavior: harness-init.sh writes a working harness into a target repo at the requested level, detects the project's real verification command, and never overwrites an existing file without --force.
verification: Run with --dry-run and confirm nothing is written.
Run --level minimal and confirm all 7 critical audit checks pass.
Run --level full and confirm the audit scores at least 70/74.
Re-run over an existing AGENTS.md and confirm it is preserved without --force.

layers.label: runtime
layers.repair: Read the first failing assertion only. Fix it, re-run. Do not batch fixes across sections.

evidence: tests/run-tests.sh sections 4-7 pass — minimal 7/7 critical, full 72/74, clobber protection confirmed 2026-08-05
features.notes: Detects npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, uv/poetry/pip, cargo and go.

features.behavior: verify-feature.sh is the only path to a passing state: it runs each layer in order, stops at the first failure with that layer's repair guidance, and records commit-stamped evidence on success.
verification: Promote a feature whose layers all pass; confirm state=passing and evidence recorded.
Fail a layer; confirm the repair text prints and the feature is NOT promoted.
Use a layer command that calls exit; confirm repair guidance still prints.

layers.label: runtime
layers.repair: Section 8 covers this gate. A failing layer must never promote a feature — that is the whole point of the script.

evidence: tests/run-tests.sh section 8 passes — all four gate behaviours confirmed 2026-08-05
features.notes: Layer commands run in a subshell so a layer calling exit cannot kill the script before it reports.

features.behavior: clean-state-check.sh and check-arch.sh block a dirty clock-out: false passing states, WIP=1 violations, stray artifacts, committed secrets and conflict markers all fail with a named fix.
verification: Mark a feature passing with no evidence; confirm clean-state-check catches it.
Activate two features; confirm the WIP=1 violation is reported.
Commit a realistic credential; confirm check-arch reports WHAT/WHY/FIX and names the file.

layers.label: runtime
layers.repair: Sections 9-10 cover these gates. If a secret rule stops firing, check the regex survives the JSON to shell round-trip — avoid nested quoting in rule commands.

features.behavior: A user can audit and harness any of their repositories without installing anything: bash, git and python3 only.
verification: Apply the kit to three real repositories.
Record the audit score before and after for each.
Confirm no repository needed a dependency install to run the audit.

layers.label: runtime
layers.repair: If the audit needs anything beyond bash/git/python3, remove the dependency — portability is the point of this kit.
